correctness.rationale: Lucas theorem gives parity from containment of binary one-bits. For even \(n\), the two binomial factors for odd \(k\) require a subset of the common one-bit set of \(n\) and \(n-1\), giving \(2^{s_2(n)-1}\) odd-position hits; symmetry doubles. For odd \(n\), successive Lucas subsets occur in \(2^{s_2(n)-t}\) blocks of length \(2^t\), each with \(2^t-1\) adjacent pairs. Dyadic histograms count unrestricted higher bits, and their geometric sums yield \(\frac{5\cdot3^{L-1}-3}{2}\) for all \(L\). Direct checker passes all rows through 128 and seven complete dyadic blocks; no inference from samples.

value.rationale: Exact complete all-index classification of a naturally recorded Narayana parity invariant and a full multiplicity-spectrum law across every dyadic row block replace the finite published census. The odd-row terminal-one-run factor reveals a structural dichotomy absent from the initial table, enabling exact distribution and cumulative counts for arbitrarily large ranges. The contribution is elementary and limited to parity, but a complete previously unreported natural invariant rather than an arbitrary slice or finite computation.
